# required-column-unique-index

- Dialects: mysql, postgres, sqlite
- Default: on

## Why

This is the required-column-unique-index violation of the required-column rule: a unique index that does not start with the required column. Some columns must be present on every table of a kind, for example a column that scopes each row to its owner. The required-column rule is configured under rules.required-column.options: column (required, the column name), tables (optional, the tables it applies to; default all) and exclude_tables (optional, tables that are skipped). Without the column option it does nothing. Each violation is reported under its own rule id, so an exclusion silences one violation only. The options are read from rules.required-column.options.

## Fix

Declare the unique index on the model with the column as its first field, and regenerate the schema.

## Exception

Tables that are shared across all owners, such as reference data or the owner table itself, when the reason is written down.

The same text is printed by `schemalens explain required-column-unique-index`. An exclusion needs a written reason. Back to the [rule index](README.md).
